In the reproducer the output is [8.0843341, 3.76166312, -2.78582009, 0.7696327, -2.78582009, 1.0], with max error 8.08433409884193. The error is platform-dependent and finicky to reproduce.

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Points differing by very small amounts, e.g. 2e-313 (subnormal range) and 1.0735703551645039e-302 in the regression test; the discrepancy appears when two y points are nearly identical.
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: np.allclose with rtol=1e-5 and atol=1e-5 in the hypothesis reproducer; the regression test expects a LinAlgError with match 'Singular matrix' rather than a numeric tolerance.
category_specific_evidence: Issue #23761 reports extreme errors at training points when two inputs are nearly identical (differing by e.g. 2e-313) with default smoothing=0, violating exact interpolation.
The issue reproducer uses points including [0.0, 2.2250738585e-313] and expects the result to match values [0,0,0,0,0,1] at the training points.
Reported error is machine-dependent: the issue states the necessary POC changes from machine to machine.
The fix replaces the general LAPACK gesv solver with symmetric sysv (dgesv changed to dsysv), since the linear system is symmetric by construction.
The regression test test_singular expects RBFInterpolator to raise LinAlgError 'Singular matrix' for the near-singular floating-point input, so the reproduction should check singularity detection.
The hypothesis reproducer checks np.allclose(result, values, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-5) on random points in [-5,5] with values in [-10,10].
reproduction_risks: The issue states the error is finicky and depends on the machine, so the reproducer may not trigger the bug on every platform.
Subnormal-range coordinates (around 1e-313) may be sensitive to floating-point handling and platform details.
The regression test expects an exception, while the random hypothesis reproducer expects numeric agreement; the two outcomes differ and must not be conflated.
The precision of the symmetric-solver fix is not stated in the passages.
